subject: ACME: intermittent WebSocket stalls under peak load — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Engineering <eng+inference@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Live inference hangs during Black Friday load spike

Hi Grace / Rachel,

We started our Black Friday stress test this morning and are seeing repeated WebSocket stalls with your streaming API. Symptoms: the connection stays open, tokens stop arriving for ~8-20s before resuming; sometimes the client receives final chunk with a 500-level error. This is impacting our user simulation; throughput drops ~30% on high concurrency.

What we've observed:
- Starts after sustained 600+ concurrent streams for ~12 minutes
- Intermittent 502 and 504 in HTTP/1.1 chunked mode and silent gaps over the WS path
- When stalls occur, latency for subsequent requests spikes and KV cache hit rate drops in our traces

I attached a short client-side capture (webrtc_clip.mp4) and a trimmed trace (acme_stream_trace.log). Our SRE has this as INC-ACME-7821. Can you advise immediate mitigations? This is high priority for the rollout.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Lead SRE, ACME Retail

--- Attachment(s): webrtc_clip.mp4 (video), acme_stream_trace.log (text)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference hangs during Black Friday load spike

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments, they're very helpful. Sorry you're seeing this during a stress run. I'm escalating to our runtime team (Dev, Markus) for immediate triage and looping Rachel for account coordination.

Immediate next steps we are taking:
- Dev will triage trace and try a hotfix to adjust WebSocket keepalive and chunk flush thresholds.
- We'll temporarily route your highest-throughput routes to a lower-latency cluster (no model change) to see if the behavior is capacity-related.
- If needed, we'll enable conservative connection throttling at the edge for ACME to stabilize stream bandwidth while we patch.

Can you confirm: is the traffic pattern using many short-lived streams (bursting) or long-lived streams that keep sending inference calls over the same connection? That affects the KV cache behavior.

I'll keep you posted every 30 minutes until this is stabilized.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME: Live inference hangs during Black Friday load spike

Samantha / Grace / team — quick triage notes after looking at acme_stream_trace.log:

Findings:
- We see repeated write stalls on the chunked-transfer path followed by long round-trip times to the dechunking worker (~12s) under sustained >500 concurrent streams.
- WS heartbeats are present but the runtime's chunk flush timer combined with the client buffer threshold is allowing long silent intervals before forcing a flush; this is exacerbated by certain concurrency patterns.
- Error bursts appear correlated with transient OOMs on a small subset of workers that then recover; when recovery happens, client sees a sudden 500 chunk.

Mitigation applied (10:00 PDT):
- Lowered server-side chunk flush interval from 1200ms -> 250ms for ACME routes (hotfix rollout, no model swap).
- Temporarily enabled earlier per-connection throttling to cap concurrent streaming requests per session to 40 to avoid pathological packing.

Request from ACME: if you can run another short stress from your end (10m at 600+ concurrency) and report if stalls persist that will validate the hotfix.

Planned follow-up:
- Patch to streaming runtime to detect and preempt worker memory pressure and fail-fast to fallback instances (Jira INF-2246).
- Longer-term: add adaptive flush/heartbeat tuning that accounts for per-route sequence length distributions.

Logs attached: trimmed runtime logs and a quick heap profile snapshot.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

--- Attachment(s): runtime_trimmed.log, heap_snapshot.txt
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: ACME: Live inference hangs during Black Friday load spike

Thanks Dev — running another 12-minute stress run now (starting 10:30 PDT). We'll push a representative workload with 650 concurrent streams and report back in 15.

Two quick asks from ACME ops:
1) If stalls persist, we will need an incident postmortem and a proposal for a mitigation that doesn't rely on throttling — throttling would materially change our UX.
2) We are going to request an SLA credit if this pattern is confirmed to be caused by runtime instability during the stress window. Please advise the process; I copied Rachel for commercial coordination.

I'll send the results shortly.

—Samantha
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-retail.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: ACME escalation summary and exec note (INF-2246)

Samantha / ACME execs — follow-up and summary from Redwood: we've validated the hotfix materially reduced silent gaps in most runs but ACME hit two residual stalls during a prolonged 1-hour ramp test last night. Details:

- Root cause (interim): interaction of chunked-transfer flush timers + worker memory pressure on workers handling long-lived multi-call streams under extreme concurrency. The hotfix reduced median silent gap from 12s -> 0.6s but did not eliminate rare 5-8s tail events.
- Action plan:
  1) Short term (next 72h): deploy a runtime patch that fails fast on worker memory pressure and routes to warm standby workers (INF-2246). We will coordinate a maintenance window with ACME.
  2) Mid term (2-4 weeks): implement adaptive flush heuristics and connection-aware batching to avoid pathological buffering on heavy multi-call sessions.
  3) Commercial: Rachel will coordinate an incident report and SLA credit request. Rachel — can you start HubSpot HS-ACME-4892 and a formal postmortem?

I've linked the engineering ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2246. Markus will lead the runtime patch work, Dev will own the rollback/failover controls, and I'll be your main contact for status and scheduling.

Samantha — thank you for the thorough traces and for running the follow-up tests. We'll provide hourly updates while the patch is progressing and plan a 1:1 with ACME leadership if the credit/procurement conversation advances.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Cc: Rachel Kim (Commercial Lead) for SLA/postmortem coordination
